newsitem.title: USA: State treasurers urged to invest in Pacific Rim.
newsitem.headline: State treasurers urged to invest in Pacific Rim.

text.p: State treasurers from across the United States were urged on Monday to capitalize on investment opportunities overseas, particularly in fast-growing Pacific Rim countries.
Hundreds of state officials attending the National Association of State Treasurers (NAST) conference heard from investment experts during the opening session in San Diego.
"We're here to look at new horizons -- to look at new investments," said Georgie Thomas, New Hampshire's treasurer and NAST's president.
Edmond Villani, president of Scudder Stevens & Clark, told state officials that market conditions were ideal for investments outside the United States, particularly in developing nations.
"Investors need to think global," Villani said.
Other experts touted opportunities for states to invest in the booming economies of the Pacific Rim.
"Any way you cut it, economists remain optimistic about economic growth in emerging Asia," Jackson Tai, a managing director at J.P. Morgan and Co Inc, told state treasurers.
Charles Valdes, chairman of the California Public Employees' Retirement System investment committee, said state officials need to develop partnerships in Asia.
"It's a global economy now," Valdes said. "You have to recognize that."
During the three-day conference, state treasurers will also attend sessions about banking, the U.S. economy, and investment opportunities in Mexico and Canada.
California state Treasurer Matt Fong will lead a delegation of treasurers on Wednesday to meet with government officials in Tijuana about trade with Mexico.
"This summit will help these states identify opportunities for investment and meet with Mexican business leaders who can help them with job-creating projects in their own state," Fong said.
Since taking office, Fong has spearheaded state efforts to promote trade and investment with Mexico and the Pacific Rim.
